summary.intent: Assess whether Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability) needed discussion before planning, clean up stale/drifted todos across Phases 70-73, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 end-to-end while the user was away for a few hours.
summary.outcome: Diagnosed and fixed three CI regressions traced to Phase 70.1/71 fallout (merged as PR #601 and #600, including a real FUSE seq-1 equivocation bug, a stale IndexedDB test helper, and multiple e2e flakes), then completed Phase 72 planning (10 plans, 6 success criteria) and executed all 10 plans sequentially, additionally fixing 113 pre-existing test-file TypeScript errors, wiring CI to typecheck test files, and finding/fixing a real DoS-class cycle-guard gap in `collectDescendantIpnsNames` — work was still finishing (committing the guard fix, agent writing the new Test D) when the transcript ends.

repo: ci-e2e.yml (Web/Desktop E2E) triggers only on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — must dispatch manually via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s if the workflow definition predates that input) to validate a fix pre-merge.

`pnpm typecheck` previously only ran each package's `build` (tsconfig.build.json, tests excluded) plus tsconfig.scripts.json — test files were never typechecked in CI, letting drift accumulate silently across phases.

`@cipherbox/*` packages resolve via workspace symlinks to built `dist` (no path aliases or TS project references), so a build-first-then-typecheck ordering is required — typecheck can't run before any package's build.

Playwright `ciFloor()` helper only raises wait timeouts under CI env var, creating a systematic local/CI asymmetry — several 'flaky' tests were actually just correct-but-slow IPNS round-trips hitting a too-tight local-only timeout.

IPNS anti-equivocation gate (Phase 71 #599) rejects same-sequence republish with a different CID (HTTP 400) — correct as a security guarantee, but broke FUSE's per-file first-publish path which republishes seq=1 with a fresh CID after rotation re-keying.

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with test/fixture drift never caught: stale desktop-e2e `.mts` DTO field names (pre-rename), a non-deterministic sdk-e2e assertion (Test 21 D-06), and the FUSE seq-1 bug — repo closes todos by deleting them from pending/, but Phase 71's 8 source todos were left stranded in pending/ despite being shipped.

`dfsFindFolder` (client.ts) threads a `visited: Set<string>` cycle guard; its sibling `collectDescendantIpnsNames` lacked one — a cyclic/malicious folder graph could hang/stack-overflow the walk (found only because a test-hardening pass tried to un-skip a placeholder test).

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the 'inode cid empty' first-publish branch; fixed by resolving IPNS first and routing a Found result into the existing CAS-retry path instead of blindly re-sealing at seq=1.

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (per Greptile P2) so a caller that already resolved the sequence (the Found path) skips a redundant second resolve round-trip; the conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after a conflict.
collectDescendantIpnsNames lacked the visited-set cycle guard present in dfsFindFolder; guard added at all three recursive call sites to prevent unbounded recursion on cyclic/malicious folder graphs.

workflow: When e2e workflows only run on push/dispatch, rebase the fix branch onto main (to include other already-merged fixes) before dispatching, so the validation run reflects the true merge state instead of a stale one.

For local reproduction of CI-only-passing tests, patch webServer.reuseExistingServer to bypass the CI-only branch and run with the CI timeout floor (ciFloor) applied locally, rather than chasing timeouts test-by-test — reverted the patch immediately after.
Sequential execution on the main tree (not git worktrees) is the reliable choice for a pnpm monorepo phase, since fresh worktrees lack node_modules and most plans serialize on one file anyway.
Stashing uncommitted bookkeeping (todo moves, ROADMAP edits) is a safe way to preserve 'do not commit yet' work when a higher-priority interrupt (CI fire) forces a branch switch.
Dispatch order for CI E2E workflows takes `--ref <branch>` and runs the workflow definition from that branch's head, not `workflow_dispatch -f ref=` with an input name.

friction: Initially checked the wrong todo directory (resolved/ instead of completed/), requiring user correction mid-turn.
gh workflow run -f ref= failed with HTTP 422 'Unexpected inputs' since main's workflow definition predated that input; had to use --ref instead.
Hook capability JSON (plan:pre fragments) contained raw newlines/control characters inside string values, breaking standard JSON parsing and requiring a custom lenient parser script.

Local web-e2e verification repeatedly cascaded on unrelated ambient flakes (4.10 batch delete, 4.11 batch move, 2.1 create-folder) before ever reaching the actual target tests (6.6.2, 8.2), costing ~6 sequential re-runs.
Setting CI=1 locally to match CI's timeout floor broke webServer reuse (reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI), requiring a temporary config patch and revert.
git commit hung/timed out due to a 1Password SSH-signing prompt (known recurring issue), requiring a manual check that the commit actually landed.
A `cat-file` check for whether todo moves were in HEAD gave a wrong/buggy result, requiring a second decisive recheck of the tree contents.

Scope grew mid-execution: pre-existing test-file TypeScript drift (113 errors, vitest v2→v3 + Phase-62 retired-type fallout) was discovered only after Wave 1 started, forcing an unplanned hardening pass plus CI wiring that wasn't in the original 10-plan scope.
